name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every PR before human review. The 30-60 second delay is a rounding error compared to the time saved catching style, docs, and simple logic errors early—humans waste far more time re-reviewing the same issues later. The trade-off is slower initial feedback, but that’s a net win because contributors fix issues once instead of multiple times. False positives exist, but they’re outweighed by the reduction in human review rounds.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s false positives aren’t the only risk—it also misses context-dependent errors humans catch instantly. A better alternative is to run it *only* on PRs that pass a 30-second human triage for scope, then measure how often its suggestions survive final review. Settle it by tracking: (1) false positive rate per PR, (2) human review time saved vs. added, and (3) merge speed with/without PR-Agent.
